page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz, the instance features 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is allocated at 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor cache configuration comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported instruction extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 extensions are absent.

The instance does not include local NVMe storage and relies entirely on network-attached block storage options. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. Performance benchmarks indicate reliable single-core capability, with average results in stress-ng single-core tests, single-threaded Gzip compression, and single-core Geekbench tasks. In contrast, multi-threaded scaling and memory throughput show limitations, placing multi-core stress-ng results, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and uncached memory bandwidth in the lower performance tiers.

From a qualitative architectural perspective, the server offers dedicated CPU allocation suited for lightweight compute tasks that do not demand extensive RAM capacity or raw disk IOPS. The 8.0 GB memory boundary limits resource-intensive applications, but the instance provides reliable baseline execution for microservices, single-threaded utilities, basic text processing, and light web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at 2.55 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. It delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs from 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of RAM, and 32 MB of L3 cache, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Built without bundled local storage, the instance uses network storage and provides 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Supported instruction sets include standard AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI hardware acceleration. Benchmark data demonstrates steady single-core execution across general compute and compression tasks, though multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth fall into lower performance brackets. This profile makes the instance appropriate for lightweight single-threaded processing, small microservices, and basic web utilities.
